Read a libTAS recording

read_ltm.Rd

Reads native LTM archives containing config.ini and inputs. Supports the positional input format through libTAS 1.3.5 and the later tagged format, including ordered input events and up to four controllers.

Usage

read_ltm(path, analog = "raw", deadzone = NULL, triggers = "raw", ...)

Arguments

path

Recording file path.

analog

Stick representation: "raw" (default), "cardinal4", "cardinal8", "angle", or "angle+magnitude". A scalar applies to both sticks; c(left = "cardinal8", right = "angle") selects them independently. Cardinal modes add separate left/right logical direction columns. Continuous modes return numeric fields through stick_channels(). Original X/Y values remain in analog_channels() in every mode. Absent sticks add no columns.

deadzone

Radial threshold in centred axis half-range units, from zero to one. One value applies to both sticks; named left/right values are allowed. NULL uses format defaults: 0.25 for BK2/PSX, 0.125 for M64/DTM. Neutral observations have no direction and an NA angle. Magnitude is kept.

triggers

"raw" (default) or "digital". For DTM, digital additionally projects each analogue trigger at 128/255 into separate L2/R2 columns. Hardware L/R click bits remain distinct from thresholded analogue triggers.

...

Reader-specific arguments, such as controller_order for M64 or DTM, or member for a recording inside a ZIP archive (see movie_members()).

Value

A replayr_movie with frame timing, source inputs, and metadata.

Details

Each row is a recorded frame. movie$timing contains framerate_num, framerate_den, duration_seconds, realtime_sec, and realtime_nsec. Frame durations follow the recorded rate changes. movie$input_events retains each frame's ordered events, and movie$flags retains emulator flags.

source_input_log retains the original input lines and their row index. Keyboard keys use their hexadecimal X KeySym in button_layout(), such as keysym_ff53 for Right. Keyboard and mouse inputs occupy player 1 alongside controller 1. Controller buttons retain gamepad identities, including L3 and R3. analog_channels() includes left_x, left_y, right_x, right_y, trigger_left, and trigger_right as signed 16-bit source values. Both sticks support the representations selected by analog. Mouse channels are mouse_x, mouse_y, mouse_wheel, and mouse_mode; mode 0 denotes absolute coordinates and mode 1 denotes relative movement. The complete configuration remains in movie$header$configuration.
